findings.description: publicly_accessible = true gives the MySQL instance a public endpoint reachable from the internet, exposing the database directly to untrusted networks and relying solely on the security group and the 'admin' master password for protection.
storage_encrypted = false leaves the RDS volume and its snapshots unencrypted, so anyone obtaining the underlying storage or a snapshot can read application data in cleartext.

findings.issue_category: master credentials in variables and state
findings.description: The master username is the well-known default 'admin' and the password comes from var.password, which is persisted in plaintext in Terraform state and re-used in EC2 user data, instead of manage_master_user_password / Secrets Manager or IAM database authentication.

The user_data script interpolates the RDS master username and var.password into /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc. User data is readable from the instance metadata service by any local process or via SSRF, and through the EC2 DescribeInstanceAttribute API, leaking the database master credentials.

The inline policy grants s3:*, ec2:* and rds:* on Resource "*" to the role attached to an internet-reachable web server; compromise of the PHP application yields near-total control of S3 data, EC2 infrastructure (a privilege-escalation path) and all RDS databases in the account.

No metadata_options block with http_tokens = "required" is set, so IMDSv1 remains available on a public-facing PHP server; an SSRF in the application could retrieve the instance profile credentials carrying the wildcard s3/ec2/rds permissions.

The bootstrap installs only httpd and serves the PHP form and query results over plain HTTP with no TLS, and the mysqli_connect call does not require SSL, so credentials and employee records traverse the network unencrypted.

No root_block_device with encrypted = true is specified, so the EBS volume containing the plaintext database credential file dbinfo.inc may be stored unencrypted depending on the AMI and account default.

Port 3306 is opened to the entire VPC CIDR rather than referencing the application server's security group, allowing any host in the VPC to reach the database; combined with publicly_accessible = true this widens the exposed surface.
The custom MySQL 8.0 parameter group does not set require_secure_transport = 1, so clients may connect to the database without TLS and transmit credentials and query data in cleartext.
The database security group permits all protocols and ports outbound to 0.0.0.0/0, providing an unconstrained data exfiltration and command-and-control path from the database tier.
